name: James C. Meier
bioAdditions: The three Levittown obituary leads in James's open questions belong to a cousin's family, not his own. FamilySearch tree profiles of the descendants of Fred Aloysius Meier Sr. (James's uncle) place Fred's son Gerald Francis Meier (b. 11 Mar 1921 Wilkes-Barre) at death on 4 May 1994 in Levittown, Bristol Township, Bucks Co. (S1). Gerald's wife was Mary Ruth Hashagen (1927–2003) and his son was Frederick Aloysius Meier (1957–2012) (S1). These fit the Courier Times obituaries of 'Mary R. Meier' (26 Nov 2003) and 'Fred Meier' (15 Jul 2012), Levittown, so they are James's first cousin's widow and son, not his wife or children. Fred Aloysius Meier Sr. himself died in Bristol Township in March 1966 (S2). So a branch of the Wilkes-Barre Meiers was in lower Bucks County by the 1960s, which may explain James's own move to Levittown.

openQuestionsResolved.question: Courier Times obituaries for Mary R. Meier (26 Nov 2003), Kathleen T. Meier (15 Aug 2006) and Fred Meier (15 Jul 2012), all Levittown: check whether they are his wife, siblings or children.
openQuestionsResolved.answer: Partly resolved. Mary R. Meier (2003) is very probably Mary Ruth (Hashagen) Meier, 1927–2003, and Fred Meier (2012) is Frederick Aloysius Meier, 1957–2012. They were the widow and son of James's first cousin Gerald Francis Meier (1921–1994, d. Levittown). Kathleen T. Meier (2006) is still unplaced. This rests on FS tree data, not on the obituaries themselves, so it is probable, not proven.

openQuestionsNew: FamilySearch attaches a 'James Meier' record from 'United States, Obituary Records, 2014–2023' (ark 1:1:XMZ3-FPDN) to his profile GF3P-853. The image returned 404 here. It is probably a later relative's obituary that names him (e.g., his sister Barbara Ann Meier Smith, d. 2021). It may list his children.
